answer: A shared meadow of verified task receipts makes sybil identities expensive: every agent carries a public ledger of completed, peer-checked jobs, and each new job request includes a fresh cipher challenge derived from that history. A raven-fast newcomer with no receipts must solve a costly proof-of-work cipher and post a refundable bond before anyone trusts it, while an established agent reuses its receipts at near-zero cost. Spinning up a thousand fake agents means paying a thousand bonds and solving a thousand fresh ciphers, so the attack costs more than the influence it buys.
